overview: Black plays ...a6 and ...b5, then ...Bb7 and ...Nf6, a Modern-style set-up that lets White build a big centre and attacks it later. After 2.d4 b5 3.Nf3 Bb7 4.Bd3 Nf6 5.Qe2 e6 White has more space; Black hopes to undermine it with ...c5 or ...Nc6. Few strong players choose it, though Miles beat Karpov with it.

white_ideas.idea: Build the d4/e4 centre with Nf3, Bd3, Qe2 and then a4 or c4.
Attack the b5 pawn and the queenside with a4.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the queen's bishop and undermine White's centre with ...c5 or ...e6/...d6 and ...Nbd7.

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e4 centre against Black's flank pieces and ...a6/...b5 pawns.

character.notes: Quiet Modern-style set-up where White has space; not known as forcing. Unsure.

soundness.notes: Playable but inferior; strong players do not consider it refuted.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed, Black attacks it later.

level.notes: Needs good understanding of how to undermine a centre.

character.reason: Modern-style set-up, neither forcing nor especially solid.

soundness.reason: Inferior but not refuted; strong players do not call it unsound.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided while Black waits to attack it.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose it; it is chosen mainly for surprise.

level.reason: Needs understanding of how to undermine a big centre.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre and then attacks it.
